Q: Environment detection: node.js or browser A:

Testing for browser environment vs Node.js

These days testing for a browser environment is as simple as testing the truthiness of document.all:

// Evaluates to true in modern web browsers including IE
var is_browser = typeof document=='object' && !Object(document && document.all) || /*@cc_on!@*/false;

In the above, Object() either returns a truthy object since all objects are truthy, or in browsers, Object() returns a falsy document.all object as per the HTML5 spec. See: Why is document.all falsy?

It all started in the '00s when popular browsers wanted to support document.all without triggering IE-specific code and were already putting such measures into place. It was soon written into the HTML5 spec and is long since supported in every modern browser including Internet Explorer 11.

The /*@cc_on!@*/false tacked on at the end is an IE-only feature that evaluates to true and is needed to make it work in IE 10 and below.

The beauty of this approach is its simplicity and that it can't be spoofed since falsy objects are limited only to a handful of browser host objects. Caveat: absence of document.all might also mean code is running in a worker that doesn't have access to the DOM.

Q: Add custom Liquid Glass navigation view like App Store Connect app? A:

Regarding the first point:

The chips have some weird background color

The background is the translucent effect that you get with .regular glass, which is the default. There is also a shadow effect with this kind of glass.

To make the items more transparent, try using .clear glass instead. There is no shadow effect with clear glass either. If you are intending to add tap gestures to the items, you might want to make the glass interactive too:

.glassEffect(.clear.interactive())

Regarding the second point:

Scrolling the list up makes it fade out below the navigation, but the chips are not taken into account

If you want the fade effect to start behind your glassy items, you just need to change it from .safeAreaInset to .safeAreaBar. The documentation has a discussion:

Similar to the safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) modifier, the content view is anchored to the specified horizontal edge of the parent view and its width insets the safe area.

Additionally, it extends the edge effect of any scroll views affected by the inset safe area.

.safeAreaBar(edge: .top) {
    ScrollView(.horizontal) {
        // ...
    }
}

Q: VSCode cannot find module '@angular/core' or any other modules A:

Delete Node Modules folder from project folder.Run below command

npm cache clean --force
npm install

It should work.
